old: From the curve, saturation is about 98% at 100 mmHg (lungs) and about 76% at 40 mmHg (tissue). The difference, roughly 98 − 76 ≈ 22%, or about 20%, is the fraction of sites that released O2. "75%" is the saturation remaining in the tissue, not the amount unloaded; the sigmoid shape means most of the O2 stays bound until the pressure falls further, as in exercising muscle.
